rubric: Do Temporal's recovery improvements justify adding a server + DB + deterministic-workflow constraints over the existing engine?

rubricApplication.recoveryImprovement: automatic re-dispatch + replay (no manual resume), and no sub-window recoverability gaps like F1/F2/F3
rubricApplication.cost: server + DB + 3 listeners + worker lifecycle + SDK + workflow versioning + determinism constraints + app-level idempotency for writer side effects (Temporal does NOT remove the writer-dedup problem; it relocates it)
rubricApplication.verdict: The improvement is real but does not offset the cost for AutoLoop's graph model: (a) AutoLoop's writer phases already fail CLOSED (0 duplicates) while Temporal's RAW semantics re-execute and duplicate unless the app writes idempotency code — the exact pattern DE-2 would add to STACK_A anyway; (b) F1/F2/F3 are bounded in-process fixes (DE-2 scope), not architectural gaps; (c) AutoLoop does not need durable timers/signals/long-running workflows (DE-1 fitNotes confirmed); (d) the operational surface grows from zero to server+DB+versioning.
